sex.evidence: Adult (8 -10 weeks) C57BL/6J and TRAP2 (Jackson, strain name Fos tm2.1(icre/ERT2)Luo /J , stock number 030323) male mice were used.

dosing.doses_raw: 1 mg/kg, i.p.; local intracerebral infusion of 5 ng or 50 ng (25 pmol or 250 pmol)
dosing.evidence: Psilocin was solubilized in a mixture of DMSO and normal saline. The test substances were administered intraperitoneally ((i.p.) at a volume of 8 mL/kg. ... microinjection of saline or psilocin (5 ng or 50 ng) into the target brain region. In TRAP2 mice psilocin (1 mg/kg, i.p.) was given for TRAP labeling, again one week before the formal session to establish baseline HTR, and again during the formal experiment.

M100907 was solubilized in a mixture of DMSO and saline to give a final concentration of 1 ng/200 nL. All injections were infused locally. ... we locally infused the 5-HT2A receptor antagonist M100907 into the mPFC prior to psilocin administration.
mice received intraperitoneal injections of 4-hydroxytamoxifen (50 mg/kg) and psilocin (1 mg/kg) to selectively activate and label neurons responsive to psychedelic stimulation.

handling.evidence: During the adaptation period, mice were allowed to move freely in the test cage for 1 h and were handled for 0.5 h daily to acclimate to the experimental environment and procedures.

assays.assay_description: Counting of head twitch events from overhead video in a test cage by two blinded observers. Variants pooled per rubric: (i) 10-min recording after local intracerebral infusion of psilocin (5 or 50 ng) or saline into mPFC, OFC, DMS or IPAC (plus M100907 pre-infusion control, Fig. S6, and Day1/Day2 control, Fig. S5); (ii) optogenetic activation of c-Fos-TRAPed mPFC neurons in TRAP2 mice (5 min laser-off baseline + 5 min stimulation at 1, 5, 20 Hz; extended 15-min 5 Hz protocol); (iii) optogenetic inhibition during systemic psilocin (1 mg/kg i.p.) with 10 alternating 1-min laser-off/laser-on cycles over 20 min.

application_type.evidence: The test substances were administered intraperitoneally ((i.p.) at a volume of 8 mL/kg ... microinjection of saline or psilocin (5 ng or 50 ng) into the target brain region.

setup_habituation.evidence: During the adaptation period, mice were allowed to move freely in the test cage for 1 h ... In the final 3 days of the adaptation period, mice were acclimated to the injector cannula insertion for 20 min daily / tethered to the optic fiber patch cable for 20 min daily.

setup_restrain.evidence: mice were allowed to move freely in the test cage

food_restriction.evidence: No food is described in the test cage; HTR was recorded by a camera mounted above the cage during short sessions.

water_restriction.evidence: No water is described in the test cage during the recording sessions.

time_to_assay.evidence: A camera mounted above the cage recorded the mice for the next 10 min after the microinjection (0 min post-infusion); 'mice were administered psilocin (1 mg/kg, i.p.). HTR was assessed for 1 min with the laser off...' (acute); optogenetic activation tests were performed ~1 week or more after the psilocin TRAP-labeling injection.

sample_size.evidence: mPFC, n = 9 mice, OFC, n = 7 mice, DMS, n = 6 mice, IPAC, n = 5 mice; optogenetic activation n = 9 mice per group; optogenetic inhibition n = 8 mice per group.

outcomes.summary: HTR was the sole behavioural readout. Local infusion of psilocin into the mPFC (5 ng, 25 pmol) significantly increased HTR, while infusion into OFC, DMS or IPAC did not; a 10-fold higher dose (50 ng) did not further increase HTR. Optogenetic activation of psilocin-TRAPed mPFC neurons induced spontaneous HTR (most robust at 5 Hz, further increased with 15-min stimulation), whereas optogenetic inhibition of those neurons reduced systemic psilocin-induced HTR by about two-thirds. Local mPFC infusion of the 5-HT2A antagonist M100907 partially reduced psilocin-induced HTR.
outcomes.statistics: Paired t test, mPFC n = 9, OFC n = 7, DMS n = 6, IPAC n = 5, ** p < 0.01 and *** p < 0.001; optogenetic activation: Paired t test, n = 9 mice per group, ** p < 0.01, **** p < 0.0001; optogenetic inhibition: Paired t test, n = 8 mice per group, ** p < 0.01, **** p < 0.0001.
outcomes.evidence: only localized infusion of psilocin into the mPFC induced a significant HTR ... administration of a minimal dose (5 ng or 25 pmol) of psilocin was sufficient to trigger substantial HTR, while a 10-fold increase in dosage did not significantly elevate the behavioral response ... optogenetic inhibition of c-Fos-positive neurons within the mPFC significantly attenuated psilocin-induced HTR.

B1_num_measures.evidence: The video recordings were analyzed by two independent observers, unaware of the treatment conditions, to count the numbers of HTR.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: HTR counts were totalled per epoch (10 min after infusion; 5 min laser-off vs 5 min laser-on; laser-on vs laser-off cycles); no within-session time-course analysis is reported.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of behavioural sequences, transitions or bout microstructure is reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: HTR used as primary behavioural readout; 'Although additional behaviors such as jumping and grooming have been observed following psychedelic administration, our study aimed to ... using HTR as the primary behavioral readout.' Per rubric, HTR is not an ethological behaviour.

B5_social.evidence: Mice were tested individually in a test cage; no social construct measured.

B6_cognitive.evidence: HTR counting involves no learning, memory, or cognitive demand.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: The video recordings were analyzed by two independent observers ... to count the numbers of HTR.

B8_multivariate.evidence: Only paired t tests on HTR counts; no multivariate or dimensionality-reduction analysis.

E1_environment_type.evidence: mice were allowed to move freely in the test cage ... A camera mounted above the cage recorded the mice.

E6_spatial.evidence: Testing took place in a single test cage filmed from above; no compartments described.

E7_social_context.evidence: Individual mice were recorded in the test cage after infusion/injection; no conspecific mentioned.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water described in the test cage during the short recording sessions.

D1_continuity.evidence: One week before the formal experimental session, mice received intraperitoneal injections of saline and psilocin (1 mg/kg) to establish baseline HTR behavior ... During the formal experiment, mice were again injected intraperitoneally with psilocin; also 'local infusion of psilocin on Day 1 has no significant interference on HTR measured on Day 2 (Figure S5)'.

D2_session_duration.evidence: HTR was assessed for 1 min with the laser off, then 1 min with the laser on ... and then repeated 10 times (total period of 20 min).

D3_recording_days.evidence: Control experiments showed that the local infusion of psilocin on Day 1 has no significant interference on HTR measured on Day 2 (Figure S5); baseline HTR session one week before the formal inhibition session.

D4_baseline.evidence: On the sixth day of the adaptation period, mice received an injection of saline (8 mL/kg, i.p.) ... One week before the formal experimental session, mice received intraperitoneal injections of saline and psilocin (1 mg/kg) to establish baseline HTR behavior (data shown in Figure 4C); in optogenetic activation 'HTR was assessed for 5 min with the laser off (baseline measure)'.

D5_followup.evidence: Control experiments showed that the local infusion of psilocin on Day 1 has no significant interference on HTR measured on Day 2 (Figure S5); optogenetic activation sessions were conducted ≥1 week after the psilocin TRAP-labeling injection.

D6_circadian.evidence: Longest session was 20 min, far under 6 h.

judge_notes: Merged the three candidate assays ('HTR – local infusion', 'HTR – optogenetic activation', 'HTR – optogenetic inhibition') into a single Head Twitch Response assay: the rubric explicitly states that the same behavioural paradigm under different routes of administration (systemic vs. intracerebral) and under optogenetic manipulations constitutes ONE assay.
Dropped c-Fos immunofluorescence quantification (Figure 1) — histological endpoint, not a behavioural assay.

B1 scored 0 (single measure, HTR count); deepseek's '2-3' was rejected because jumping/grooming were explicitly NOT quantified and laser-on vs laser-off counts are the same variable under different conditions.
D2 scored 1 (15–60 min): the optogenetic inhibition session was a continuous 20-min recording (10 × 1 min off / 1 min on), longer than the 10-min infusion and 15-min activation bouts.

D4 scored 1: Figure 4C reports HTR after saline injection one week before the psilocin formal session, and the activation experiment includes a 5-min laser-off baseline; D5 scored 1 on the basis of the Day1/Day2 control (Figure S5) and the ≥1-week interval between the TRAP-labeling psilocin dose and optogenetic testing.
Dosing schedule set to 'repeated' (overriding all candidates' 'acute') because TRAP2 mice received psilocin (1 mg/kg i.p.) for TRAP labeling, again for baseline HTR, and again in the formal session.
Added M100907 and 4-hydroxytamoxifen as additional compound entries since both were administered to animals in the behavioural experiments.
